dedupe_keys.name: dieterpy python gams framework for the dieter power sector model

description: DIETERpy is a Python framework for the open-source power sector optimisation model DIETER (Dispatch and Investment Evaluation Tool with Endogenous Renewables), developed by the Transformation of the Energy Economy research group at DIW Berlin. DIETER was built to study the role of electricity storage and sector coupling in future scenarios with high shares of renewable energy. DIETERpy adds pre- and post-processing of model data, scenario analysis and visualisation, and calls the GAMS optimisation routine, which is maintained separately as DIETERgms. The documentation names Carlos Gaete-Morales (lead), Alexander Roth, Martin Kittel and Wolf-Peter Schill as developers, with Alexander Zerrahn. Version 0.3 project templates on Zenodo include a base project with a hydrogen module and examples with input data. Coverage is set by the input data; applications listed focus on Germany and Europe. The code is accessible on GitLab and PyPI under the MIT licence at no cost, and DIETER input data are under CC BY-SA 4.0. Caveats: a GAMS licence and solver are needed, and the latest GitLab release is v1.6.2 from August 2023. Simulation uses are least-cost capacity expansion and hourly dispatch with storage, hydrogen and flexible demand. Related records: model-powergenome prepares inputs for capacity expansion models, and model-eltramod-stud is another European power market model.
